notes:
User is planning a dinner party with a multicultural menu featuring Korean BBQ beef, Middle Eastern falafel, and Indian dishes, prioritizing food that is easy to prepare in large quantities. They considered Korean options such as bulgogi, galbi, dak galbi, pork belly, japchae, and stews, plus kimchi, bokkeumbap, and other banchan. Their current Korean choices are kimchi and bokkeumbap. They asked how to make falafel crispy outside and fluffy inside. They also asked about popular Korean noodle dishes to make at home, including naengmyeon, ramyeon, jjajangmyeon, japchae, kalguksu, and haemultang.

For the Indian portion, they considered chana masala, palak paneer, samosas, tandoori chicken, vegetable biryani, rogan josh, and sag aloo, and selected samosas and saag aloo. They debated basmati brands and whether authentic Japanese short-grain rice they already use would work, but decided to buy traditional Indian basmati rice. They also mentioned hearing good things about a newly opened neighborhood Indian restaurant’s chicken tikka masala, but its name/location has not been provided.

User is interested in Korean restaurants and has tried four: one had excellent bibimbap, another very spicy kimchi jjigae, and a third had distinctive, tasty Japchae made with sweet potato noodles. They appreciate regional/preparation variations and unique restaurant styles. No dietary restrictions, guest count, city, or exact restaurant details have been specified.
